Without an input bottleneck, assuming exact affine recovery of the noisy patch from the model representation, we characterize how the covariance spectrum of corrections beyond linear denoising determines the width required above the patch dimension. ImageNet experiments with JiT show that measured denoising losses reflect the predicted bottleneck floor and its attenuation or cancellation through preconditioning. Further widening yields larger relative denoising gains at low noise, where corrections beyond linear denoising spread across more directions, consistent with our spectral characterization of the required model width. Together, these results provide a denoising-based account of practical generation-quality gaps across prediction targets, preconditioning choices, and model widths.

title: OptiCom : A Unified Framework for State-Conditioned Composition in LLM-Driven Optimization
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed to solve complex scientific and practical problems via iterative optimization. However, dynamically coordinating diverse search mechanisms as candidate quality, failure modes, and resource budgets evolve remains a critical open challenge. Targeted empirical diagnostics reveal that mechanism effectiveness is highly state-dependent. Motivated by this, we analyze how individual decisions drive final outcomes, decomposing the expected terminal improvement under a shared budget into cumulative decision opportunities minus cumulative selection losses. Guided by this opportunity-loss theoretical foundation, we propose OptiCom, a unified framework that represents LLM-driven optimizers within a shared configuration space: C=(A,Q,O,E,M,S), corresponding to artifact, query, operator, evaluation, memory, and strategy. Operating within this space, a fast LLM-based Optimization Controller dynamically composes immediate mechanisms through structured Action Packages, while a slower Strategy Adapter refines long-term selection preferences, operator weights, and templates based on accumulated trajectory feedback. Comprehensive evaluations across 32 benchmark groups demonstrate the superiority of framework: OptiCom achieves an average Max-score rank of 1.72 among 14 evaluated configurations, securing the top score in 23 groups. Ultimately, these results highlight the broad applicability and high extensibility of OptiCom as a general-purpose paradigm for robust LLM test-time scaling.

title: Minimum attaining operators on reducing subspaces: Spectral structure and density
abstract: In this article, we introduce and study the class $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$ of minimum attaining operators on a separable Hilbert space $H$ whose restrictions to every nonzero reducing subspace are minimum attaining. This class lies between the classes of absolutely minimum attaining operators and minimum attaining operators. We establish a spectral characterization of positive operators in $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$: a positive operator $T$ belongs to $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$ if and only if $T=\sum_{λ\inΛ}λP_λ$, where $Λ\subseteq[0,\|T\|]$ is a countable well-ordered set, $(P_λ)_{λ\inΛ}$ is a family of mutually orthogonal nonzero projections, and $\sum_{λ\inΛ}P_λ=I$ in the strong operator topology. We also establish a connection between $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$ and the class of operators attaining their norm on every nonzero reducing subspace. Further, we obtain stability results under suitable finite-rank and compact perturbations, and prove that $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$ is norm dense in $\mathcal{B}(H)$. We also establish the norm density of operators in this class having a nontrivial invariant half-space. Finally, we characterize normal operators in $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$, obtain a corresponding characterization for multiplication operators on $L^2(\mathbb{T})$, and characterize the condition $\mathcal{R}_T=\mathcal{R}_{|T|}$ in terms of the von Neumann algebra generated by $|T|$, showing that this condition forces $T$ to be normal.

title: Agreement Between Reconstructed and Native GDELT GKG Records: A Field-Level Baseline
abstract: The Global Knowledge Graph (GKG) of the Global Database of Events, Language, and Tone (GDELT) characterizes news articles using named entities, topics, quantitative and temporal features, quotations, tone, and dictionary-based content measures. Its codebook defines the record format, but the software that produces the records is not public, so researchers cannot generate compatible records for articles they collect themselves. We built an open-source reconstruction, gdelt-regkg, and measured how closely it agrees with GDELT's archived (native) records for 193,550 English articles from 8,729 publishers (2020-2025) and 2,500 articles in five other languages. Agreement depends strongly on the field. English tone, the percentage of positive minus negative words, has a mean absolute error (MAE) of 1.79 points and a concordance correlation coefficient of 0.75. Identity agreement (F1) is 0.65 for persons, 0.42 for organizations, and 0.65 for locations. It is lower for date components (0.42), complete counts with their objects and locations (0.07), and quotations (0.07), while GCAM category presence reaches micro F1 0.84 within the implemented dictionaries. In subsets where retrieved and native titles and lengths match, tone error falls to 1.47 and organization F1 rises to 0.48, yet most disagreement remains. A larger gazetteer raises coverage of native places from 89.5% to 97.1% with little change in location F1. Tone computed on English translations of non-English articles is less accurate (MAE 2.10-2.64) than for English articles. The results are conditional on article pages that could still be retrieved, and the correspondence subsets do not isolate the effect of input differences. Reconstructed records should therefore be assessed field by field and not treated as completely interchangeable with native ones.

title: RepoTrace: Improving Requirement Tracing in Multi-Round Agent Interactions
abstract: Code agents have become increasingly capable of performing software engineering tasks through interaction with software environments. However, agents tend to degrade as the number of interaction rounds increases, making it difficult to maintain existing software during iterative modification. We analyze 2,656 agent trajectories in EvoCode-Bench and identify requirement focus misalignment as a recurring failure pattern, where agents struggle to distinguish the primary modification targets of a requirement from unrelated code. We propose Repotrace a requirement-driven repository understanding harness that combines repository structure with requirement semantics to construct a requirement-code correspondence and injects it into the agent context. This correspondence enables code agents to follow the repository architecture, trace requirements across multi-round interactions, and identify the core code elements corresponding to the current requirement. Experiments show that Repotrace improves the mean per-round reward (MPR) across different models (e.g., +19.99 on GLM-5.2) and agent harnesses (e.g., +10.22 on Claude Code). Across rounds, Repotrace increases the average per-round reward from 0.163 to 0.371 on Terminus-2 with DeepSeek-V4-Pro, while reducing average regression errors by 56.78%. We release the source code and agents' trajectories to support future research.

title: Self-Supervised Pretraining for PHM: What Transfers, What Does Not, and What Federating It Costs
abstract: Self-supervised pretraining has produced capable time-series foundation models, but its value for Prognostics and Health Management (PHM) has not been measured under leakage-controlled conditions. We measure it on a corpus of 47 public PHM datasets, harmonized to a single tensor contract and partitioned so that 11 datasets are withheld from pretraining in full. Transfer turns out to be task-dependent: a compact channel-independent Transformer encoder (801,808 parameters) pretrained with masked patch prediction raises fault-classification macro-F1 from 0.350 to 0.812 on CWRU and from 0.569 to 0.951 on HSG18, yet on CMAPSS remaining-useful-life estimation no pretrained checkpoint reliably improves upon a from-scratch baseline. We pretrain under two regimes---centralized, and simulated cross-silo federated with ten clients grouped by physical domain---holding architecture, objective, source data and optimization budget fixed. Two further findings are negative. At matched budget the centralized encoder leads by 15.5--20.2 macro-F1 points in four of four comparisons, although the comparison is confounded by a learning-rate schedule that favours the centralized arm and rests on a single pretraining run per regime; on RUL the two regimes are indistinguishable. And the intrinsic SSL loss is not a valid selection criterion: the centralized encoder more than halves the federated reconstruction loss without a corresponding gap on RUL, and a server-momentum sweep moves downstream validation macro-F1 by up to 0.29 while the SSL loss varies by 0.021. Transfer also hinges on the backbone learning rate: the same checkpoint yields 0.169 or 0.829 macro-F1 on CWRU depending on a single order of magnitude. We release the corpus pipeline, the protocol and the code.

title: MechAlign: Evaluating Semantic Alignment at the Project Level in Mathematical Formalization
abstract: Lean verifies that a formal proof establishes its stated proposition under declared assumptions, but does not check whether that proposition faithfully expresses the mathematical claim in a manuscript. Assessing this correspondence requires interpreting the main theorem through its project dependencies, which may be scattered throughout a large development. We introduce MechAlign, a framework for project-level semantic alignment review that combines formal dependency extraction with LLM-based assessment. Its extraction tool, LeanTrace, constructs a statement dependency graph from elaborated declarations, retaining definition bodies and structure constraints while excluding proof bodies and stopping at an explicit library boundary. The reviewer uses this context to investigate alignment and report discrepancies with localized evidence. We conduct a preliminary review of 201 main results from 173 OpenAI Math projects, using supplied informal descriptions and available paper context. A hyperbolic-group case illustrates how dependency inspection localizes a missing dimensional constraint relative to the manuscript, consistent with the upstream declaration of formalization scope. We also construct LeanReviewBench, comprising 501 fixed claim-statement-context triples from OpenAI Math, Fermat's Last Theorem, and Kakeya, with description provenance recorded. The resource supports controlled comparisons of more project-level semantic alignment evaluations.

title: Efficient Exact Unlearning for Federated Zeroth-Order Optimization
abstract: Federated zeroth-order optimization (FedZOO) reduces the memory and communication costs of collaborative training for edge intelligence by avoiding backpropagation while communicating only random seeds and scalar coefficients. However, existing methods lack efficient mechanisms for exact unlearning to fully remove the influence of training data when users request deletion. A key insight is that total variation stability of the learning algorithm creates overlap between model distributions before and after data deletion, allowing exact unlearning to reuse computation through coupling. Based on this observation, we jointly design two stable zeroth-order learning algorithms and their corresponding exact-unlearning procedures: \textsc{FedZOO-S} obtains stability through client and mini-batch subsampling, enabling \textsc{FedZOUL-S} to perform efficient unlearning by preserving earlier updates and restarting from the first affected step. \textsc{FedZOO-NS} further combines subsampling with Gaussian noise to increase overlap between update distributions; \textsc{FedZOUL-NS} exploits this overlap through rejection--reflection coupling to reuse affected updates when the coupling is accepted. We prove exact unlearning for both algorithms: the model and saved state have the same joint distribution as retraining with the corresponding learner on retained data. We further establish stability and convergence guarantees for the learning algorithms and derive upper bounds on expected unlearning cost. Experiments demonstrate effective unlearning with competitive model utility and up to $56.1\%$ less cumulative unlearning time than re-optimization. Compared with first-order baselines, our methods reduce communication overhead by up to approximately four orders of magnitude.

title: Structural taxonomy and complex irreducible representations of non-abelian groups of order p^4
abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $G$ be a non-abelian group of order $p^4$. The classification of groups of order $p^4$ provides a natural setting for studying the structure of their complex group algebras. In this paper, we consider a non-abelian group G of order $p^4$ and determine the primitive central idempotents of the complex group algebra $\mathbb{C}G$. Using these idempotents, we obtain the corresponding decomposition of $\mathbb{C}G$ into simple components and describe the irreducible representations of $G$. The results provide an explicit description of the representation-theoretic structure of the chosen non-abelian group of order $p^4$ and illustrate the role of primitive central idempotents in the Wedderburn decomposition of its complex group algebra.

title: On Cayley Graphs of Skew Braces and Their Distances
abstract: We introduce the left and right Cayley graphs of a finite skew brace $(A,\cdot, \circ)$ with a connection set $T\subset A$, as a directed multigraph with additive and multiplicative edges, depicting the operations $\cdot$ and $\circ$ respectively. We compute the distance from $a$ to $a\circ b$ in these Cayley graphs in terms of factorization lengths over $T$. As an application, we provide a characterization of the ideals of a skew brace in terms of their corresponding Cayley graphs.

title: Complete characterization of internal-external entanglement trade-offs in two-mode Gaussian states
abstract: We characterize the exact trade-off between internal and external entanglement in asymmetric two-mode Gaussian states at fixed local symplectic eigenvalues. Internal entanglement is quantified by the negativity $\mathcal{N}_{A:B}$ between the two modes, while external entanglement is quantified by the negativity $\mathcal{N}_{AB:CD}$ across a Gaussian purification. Numerical sampling suggests the boundary structure of the attainable region in the $(\mathcal{N}_{AB:CD},\mathcal{N}_{A:B})$ plane, which we then determine analytically. Parametrizing the global symplectic spectrum yields a closed admissible interval for the remaining spectral parameter at fixed $\mathcal{N}_{AB:CD}$. We prove constructively that every point in this interval corresponds to a physical covariance matrix, implying that all intermediate values of $\mathcal{N}_{A:B}$ between the resulting sharp bounds are achievable. The upper bound is attained for opposite-sign correlations of equal magnitude, while the positive branch of the lower bound occurs when one global symplectic eigenvalue equals unity. We also identify two external-entanglement thresholds, derive a saturated monogamy-type inequality, and recover the symmetric-state limit. Because the external negativity depends only on the spectrum of the reduced two-mode state, the bounds hold for any purification, including non-Gaussian purifications.

title: Further Study of p-Ary Self-Orthogonal Codes From Square Functions
abstract: In this paper, we investigate a family of trace codes over finite fields of odd characteristic defined by two quadratic trace conditions. By analyzing the quadratic forms associated with these trace conditions and evaluating the corresponding character sums, we obtain the parameters and complete weight distributions of the codes. We further exploit the natural multiplicative orbit structure of the defining sets to obtain punctured codes and determine their parameters, weight distributions and dual distances. Moreover, we establish self?orthogonality criteria and investigate divisibility and projectivity of the constructed codes. These results give a unified treatment for arbitrary odd prime fields and for extension degrees of both parities.

title: The monotone part of Chatterjee's rank correlation
abstract: Chatterjee's rank correlation $ξ$ measures how strongly a random variable $Y$ depends functionally on a random variable $X$, but it does not distinguish increasing, decreasing and non-monotone relationships. We ask how much of the dependence measured by $ξ$ is explained by an increasing relationship. For continuous marginals, $ξ$ is, up to a factor, a squared distance from independence in a Hilbert space geometry derived from the Sobolev scalar product for copulas. We answer it by the metric projection onto the closed convex set of stochastically increasing copulas in this geometry. The projection is explicit: it replaces every vertical section by its least concave majorant, and it coincides with the smallest stochastically increasing copula dominating the given one. It splits $ξ$ orthogonally into a monotone part $ξ^{\uparrow}$ and the squared distance to the class of stochastically increasing copulas; dually, $ξ^{\uparrow}$ is, up to a factor, the squared distance to the polar cone, which corresponds to negative quadrant dependence. The monotone part vanishes exactly for negatively quadrant dependent copulas, equals $ξ$ exactly for stochastically increasing copulas, and equals one only for the comonotonicity copula. In contrast to $ξ$, it is increasing in the concordance order and continuous with respect to weak convergence. Symmetrisation decomposes the measure of mutual complete dependence in the same way. Finally, the construction extends to arbitrary distributions via isotonic regression of conditional distribution functions. In particular, the plug-in estimator based on the empirical distribution is strongly consistent for every copula, without smoothing or tuning parameters.

title: Evaluating Harmful Memorization in LLM Code Generation
abstract: Assessing memorization in LLM code generation is challenging because code reuse is not inherently harmful. Correct programs often share APIs, templates, and algorithmic idioms, so code similarity alone may reflect benign reuse rather than problematic memorization. We focus on the harmful case: a model fails to adapt when task semantics change and instead produces code that remains highly similar to the original solution. We propose \emph{code rewriting}, an automated semantic perturbation pipeline that constructs superficially similar but semantically different variants of existing coding tasks by modifying a core logic element of the reference solution and regenerating the corresponding prompt. To summarize this behavior, we introduce the \emph{Harmful Memorization Index} (HMI), an operational diagnostic that combines similarity to the original solution with performance degradation on rewritten tasks. We use harmful memorization as an operational behavioral term for this specific failure mode; HMI does not establish whether an original task or solution appeared in a model's training data. HMI is intended to complement standard accuracy metrics by capturing brittleness under small semantic changes. Across MBPP+ and BigCodeBench, we find that: (1) HMI does not monotonically increase with model scale and often decreases on simpler tasks; (2) high-HMI failures are concentrated in specific logic-edit types, especially constraint changes and data transformations; (3) supervised fine-tuning improves original-task accuracy but can substantially increase HMI on held-out tasks; and (4) across the evaluated post-training settings, PPO yields a more favorable accuracy--HMI trade-off than SFT.

title: Subspace-Protected Topological Phases and Bulk-Boundary Correspondence
abstract: While tremendous research has revealed that symmetry enriches topological phases of matter, more general principles that protect topological phases have yet to be explored. In this Letter, we elucidate the roles of subspaces in free-fermionic topological phases. A subspace property for Hamiltonians enables us to define new topological invariants. It results in peculiar topological boundary phenomena, i.e., the emergence of an unpaired zero mode or zero-winding skin modes, characterizing subspace-protected topological phases. We establish and demonstrate the bulk-boundary correspondence in subspace-protected topological phases. We further discuss the interplay of the subspace property and internal symmetries. Toward application, we also propose possible platforms possessing the subspace property.

title: Real-Space Interference from Quantum Metric
abstract: Real-space interference of wave packets is governed by their central momentum separation and momentum width, which set the oscillation wavelength and spatial envelope, respectively. Here, we show that in crystalline systems, quantum metric distribution in an isolated band can similarly give rise to real-space interference through the evanescent tails of a localized bound state. The location and width of a quantum metric hot spot in the momentum space set a complex wavevector as one evanescent plane wave component of a bound state. Consequently, with multiple quantum metric hot spots, the density distribution of a bound state or the total density of two spatially overlapped bound states exhibits an interference pattern, where the oscillation period and long-range decay length are determined by the momentum-space separation of the hot spots and the width of the narrowest hot spots, respectively. This quantum-geometric interference is particularly pronounced in (nearly) flat bands, where competing scales from band dispersion are suppressed. Furthermore, we demonstrate that using a Josephson STM the real-space interference can be experimentally observed through the tip-position dependence of the Josephson critical current. Our results reveal a direct correspondence between momentum-space quantum geometry and real-space interference, showing how bound-state profiles encode the momentum-resolved quantum metric.

title: SLVR: Structured Latent Visual Reasoning via Human-like Reasoning Flows
abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) often answer visual reasoning questions by relying on linguistic priors rather than task-relevant visual evidence. Textual chain-of-thought reasoning can partially mitigate this issue by encouraging models to decompose visual questions into intermediate evidence-seeking steps, but generating these steps autoregressively increases inference cost. Latent reasoning avoids explicit rationale generation, but existing approaches provide limited control over what intermediate states encode, making it difficult to impose separate supervision for planning, grounding, and evidence selection. We propose Structured Latent Visual Reasoning (SLVR), a training framework that bridges explicit chain-of-thought and latent reasoning by organizing multimodal reasoning into typed latent stages for planning, grounding, evidence selection, and reasoning integration. SLVR first trains the model to rely on the image by masking answer-revealing text and contrasting the correct answer with visually plausible distractors. It then organizes reasoning into latent stages for planning, grounding, evidence selection, and integration, supervising each stage with the corresponding signal: plans, boxes, visual evidence, and final rationales. This gives latent reasoning an explicit functional structure while avoiding generated textual chains at inference time. Built on Qwen2.5-VL-7B, SLVR improves consistently across multimodal reasoning benchmarks, with absolute gains of +9.4 on MMVP and +14.2 on BLINK Relation, as well as improvements on V*, MathVista, and ChartQA. These results suggest that structured latent supervision can improve fine-grained visual reasoning without the decoding overhead of textual CoT. Project page is available \href{https://bogao-code.github.io/SLVR/}{here}.

title: Universal polynomials for Gromov-Witten invariants on toric surfaces
abstract: We study the polynomiality of combined logarithmic and ordinary Gromov-Witten invariants with a Lambda class insertion on toric surfaces $Δ(\mathbf{c},\mathbf{d})$. We show that the combined logarithmic Gromov-Witten invariants can be expressed in terms of universal relative node polynomials when the direction vector $\mathbf{c}$ and length vector $\mathbf{d}$ of the $h$-transverse lattice polygon $Δ(\mathbf{c},\mathbf{d})$ are sufficiently large and spread out. In particular, when the normal fan of the $h$-transverse lattice polygon $Δ(\mathbf{c},\mathbf{d})$ is smooth and its edges satisfy a length condition, we show that the combined Gromov-Witten invariants are equal to a universal node polynomial. We also show that the higher genus Block-Göttsche polynomials of smooth toric surfaces corresponding to these $h$-transverse lattice polygons, including toric blowups beyond Hirzebruch and toric del Pezzo surfaces, are equal to a generating function of higher genus Gromov-Witten invariants.

title: Interpreting LLM Scores in Peer Review: Alignment and Divergence Across Prompts, Domains, and Manuscript Features
abstract: Large language model (LLM) scores are being studied as information for scholarly evaluation. Interpreting these scores requires evidence about agreement with human judgments and its variation across evaluation conditions. Guided by an argument-based approach to validation, we compare four LLMs on 7,083 public ICLR 2024 submissions under a standard review condition and examine ten prompt conditions using DeepSeek-V3.2. We distinguish average score divergence, paper-level absolute error, and rank correlation, then examine domain differences and adjusted manuscript-feature associations. For DeepSeek-V3.2, Area Chair guidance reduces mean rating divergence from 1.460 to 0.199 points and mean absolute error from 1.577 to 0.942, while rank correlation changes from 0.377 to 0.387. Historical references combined with downward scoring instructions yield mean divergence of 0.052 and rank correlation of 0.321. Domain differences remain after global calibration. Longer titles have positive adjusted associations with rating divergence, and formula density has negative associations across all four configurations. These findings connect score interpretation to the scoring procedure, evaluation context, and manuscript information represented in the comparison. They show why aggregate alignment, manuscript ordering, and correspondence within manuscript groups require distinct evidence when evaluating LLM-generated scholarly assessment information.

title: WRF-JAX v1.1.28: a differentiable regional weather model with fully coupled physics, numerically consistent with WRF and matching 128-process CPU performance on a single GPU
abstract: Porting a regional weather model in its entirety to a graphics processing unit (GPU) requires complete implementation of the dynamical core and all physical processes, and improved computational efficiency. This paper introduces WRF-JAX v1.1.28, a JAX reimplementation of the WRF 4.5 dynamical core and the complete CONUS physics suite. We conducted 27 ten-day integrations across nine regions and three initialization months, with a horizontal grid spacing of 3 km and $700\times700$ grid points, and established two numerical-difference baselines. The full-field RMSEs of wind, temperature, and moisture in WRF-JAX and the WRF internal numerical-difference baseline showed similar long-term evolution: the medians of the case-wise RMSE ratios were 1.05-1.07 at 24 h and 1.02-1.04 at 240 h. The mean sustained integration time on a single NVIDIA A800 was 175.0 s per model hour, corresponding to speedups of 1.17 and 1.05 relative to 128-process single-precision WRF runs compiled with gfortran and ifort, respectively. The experiments further backpropagated through 100 steps with full physics coupling, obtaining all three-dimensional gradient components of the initial UVTQ fields in a single calculation. The full-field Gaussian random-direction evaluation used 500 directions and three perturbation amplitudes per variable; the median relative differences in directional derivatives for zonal wind, meridional wind, dry potential temperature, and water vapour were 2.58-5.22%, 2.94-6.49%, 7.86-10.06%, and 3.51-3.91%, respectively. WRF-JAX combines fully coupled forecasting with differentiation across time steps, providing computable approximate gradients for regional weather simulation and end-to-end optimization, with accuracy comparable to that of the original WRF model and a forward integration speed equivalent to that of the original WRF model running on at least 128 cores.

title: Kronecker-Structured Video Completion with Cross-Fitted Self-Supervised Residual Learning
abstract: Tube-wise video completion reconstructs temporal trajectories at spatial locations unobserved in every frame. We propose a two-stage framework combining regularized masked Kronecker product decomposition (KPD) with cross-fitted self-supervised residual learning. First, we estimate a compact structural backbone directly from observed entries using cyclic component-wise least-squares updates, spatial and temporal factor regularization, and regularizer-optimal scale balancing. The exact updates yield a nonincreasing objective. Second, we address the mismatch between in-sample fitting errors and the prediction errors encountered at missing tubes. We partition observed tubes into folds and construct residual targets using backbone models fitted without the corresponding target tubes. A lightweight 3-D convolutional neural network then predicts corrections from the backbone, visible residual context, observation mask, and local detail features. Exact data consistency preserves observed measurements. Experiments include ablations, sensitivity analysis, grayscale and RGB video completion, and structured missing patterns. Our method achieves the highest mean PSNR and SSIM at the higher tested sampling rates on the grayscale benchmark. On eight selected DAVIS RGB sequences, it achieves the highest mean missing-region PSNR and full-frame SSIM and the lowest mean missing-tube temporal-gradient MAE at every evaluated sampling rate.

title: Type-II Singularities of Immersed Locally Convex Curves Evolving under Generalized Anisotropic Gage Area-Preserving Flows with Slow Curvature Speeds
abstract: In this paper, we study the singularity behavior of immersed locally convex closed plane curves evolving under generalized anisotropic Gage area-preserving flows with slow curvature speeds of the form $κ_σ^α$, where $0<α\le 1$. Here $κ_σ$ denotes the anisotropic curvature associated with a prescribed anisotropy function $σ$. We prove that every finite-time blow-up is of Type-II provided that the Euclidean length of the evolving curve remains uniformly bounded away from zero. This result holds without any symmetry assumptions on either the initial curve or the anisotropy. When the initial signed area is nonzero, this length lower bound is automatically satisfied, and thus any finite-time singularity is necessarily of Type-II. By means of Hamilton's rescaling method combined with a differential Harnack estimate, we show that along a suitable blow-up subsequence, the rescaled curves at the selected times converge locally to the profile of a translating solution of the corresponding anisotropic curvature flow $V=κ_σ^α$. We also establish sufficient conditions for finite-time singularity formation in terms of the initial signed area and anisotropic length. Moreover, we construct locally convex initial curves arbitrarily close to the Wulff curve for which a finite-time Type-II singularity occurs.

title: Supercritical Geometric Optics for multidimensional scalar conservation laws
abstract: This article studies the propagation, near a smooth non-constant ground state, of monophase oscillatory wave trains with small amplitude and very high frequency for multidimensional nonlinear scalar conservation laws. These oscillations lie beyond the classical regime of uniformly bounded variation. Two scenarios may occur. Under suitable compatibility conditions, the oscillations propagate. Otherwise, they are damped through shock formation. In the baseline supercritical regime, we give an explicit criterion distinguishing these two behaviors and justify the corresponding asymptotic descriptions. At higher frequencies, the propagation mechanism becomes more restrictive and is governed by compatibility conditions involving a Lie algebra. Under a natural local constant-rank assumption, we obtain a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of complete WKB expansions. We also prove cancellation under first-order incompatibility. Perturbing a non-constant background state limits the propagation of small scales compared with the constant-background case. Our constructions contribute to the understanding of the fractional smoothing effect conjectured by Lions, Perthame and Tadmor.

title: Inverse heat source problem from terminal data on a set of low Hausdorff dimension
abstract: We study the recovery of a spatial source in the heat equation from terminal observations on a compact interior set $E$ with positive $β$ dimensional Hausdorff content for some $β>d-1$. The prescribed temporal forcing vanishes on a nontrivial interval immediately preceding the observation time. Under a spectral Sobolev prior and a quantitative noncancellation condition on the terminal spectral multipliers, we establish conditional logarithmic stability. For scattered observations on such sets, we derive a sampling inequality under a quasi uniformity assumption. Under explicit sampling and independent noise assumptions, we prove a logarithmic convergence rate in probability for the corresponding Tikhonov reconstructions with a data driven parameter choice. Two numerical experiments using a finite candidate approximation of a fixed Hausdorff set assess discrete spectral sampling stability and illustrate the effects of the waiting interval and measurement noise on reconstruction.

title: Exact solutions for static spherically symmetric spacetime with a perfect fluid in Rastall theory
abstract: In general relativity, exact Liouvillian solutions for a static and spherically symmetric spacetime with a perfect fluid and the equation of state $p(r)=wρ(r)$ are known only for $w=0,-\frac{1}{6}, -\frac{1}{5}, -\frac{1}{3}$, and $-1$. We extend this setup to Rastall theory, presenting the relation between the Rastall parameter and the constant $w$, and deriving exact solutions that correspond to their known counterparts in general relativity, except for $w=-\frac{1}{6}$. Furthermore, we find that, when $w\neq \frac{1}{3}, -1$, there exist several types of solutions whose behaviors change depending on the choice of constants.

title: Gating and Learnable Temperature for Graph Attention Mechanisms
abstract: Graph attention networks learn neighbor importance through data-dependent coefficients, but standard layers lack explicit control over unreliable feature dimensions and use fixed sharpness of attention coefficient distributions. This paper proposes gated graph attention and learnable temperature for common graph attention mechanisms. Gated graph attention filters feature or message responses to reduce the influence of unreliable dimensions, while learnable temperature dynamically adjusts the sharpness of the attention coefficient distribution. We conduct experiments on five standard node classification benchmarks and five heterophilic benchmarks. On most of these benchmarks, our two modifications improve upon the corresponding graph attention backbones, and combining them can yield further gains. Controlled noise experiments further verify the behavior of the proposed mechanisms under feature perturbations. Theoretical analysis explains these results by showing that gating improves robustness when only part of the feature coordinates are reliable, while temperature is beneficial when global noise weakens the discriminability of node features.

title: Raman Signatures of Lithium Ion Dynamics in LLZO Garnet Electrolytes: Atomistic Insights from MD-Raman Calculations
abstract: Lithium lanthanum zirconate (LLZO) garnets are among the most promising solid electrolytes for next-generation batteries owing to their high ionic conductivity, chemical stability, and compatibility with lithium metal. Raman spectroscopy is commonly employed to distinguish the highly conductive cubic phase from the poorly conductive tetragonal phase of LLZO, yet the atomistic origin of these spectral differences and their direct connection to Li-ion transport remain unresolved. Here, we close this gap by comparing computed and experimental Raman spectra for the tetragonal, cubic, and Ta-doped variants of LLZO, with the computed spectra obtained from the MD-Raman approach that combines machine-learning molecular dynamics with first-principles polarizability calculations. We show that the contrasting ionic transport behavior across these LLZO variants is encoded in the vibrational dynamics of the lithium sublattice and gives rise to distinct features in their Raman spectra. A symmetry-resolved analysis further reveals that experimentally observed Raman peaks do not correspond to individual normal modes, but instead arise from overlapping contributions of multiple symmetry channels, challenging conventional peak-assignment approaches. By explicitly connecting experimentally accessible Raman signatures to the underlying atomic-scale dynamics, our results show how Raman spectroscopy can move beyond empirical phase identification toward a microscopic probe of Li-ion dynamics in lithium garnet electrolytes.

title: Power spectrum of longitudinal-velocity residuals in the Galactic disk from Gaia DR3 red-giant-branch stars
abstract: Non-axisymmetric structures in the Galaxy produce coherent stellar motions in the Galactic disk. These motions are usually interpreted by assuming parameterized gravitational potentials or specific perturbation models, thereby entangling direct kinematic information with model-dependent assumptions. Using Gaia DR3 astrometry, we analyze the Galactic longitudinal-velocity residuals of nearly four million red-giant-branch stars over $-4 < X_h < 4\, \mathrm{kpc}$ and $-6 < Y_h < 6\, \mathrm{kpc}$ in the heliocentric region. We construct an empirical axisymmetric baseline without introducing any dynamical model, and compute the power spectrum of the residual velocity field. The spectrum exhibits a broad peak at spatial frequency of $f \simeq 0.12 - 0.22\, \mathrm{kpc}^{-1}$, corresponding to a scale of around $5-8\, \mathrm{kpc}$. The residual amplitude is sensitive to the adopted distance scale: inverse-parallax distances $d_\varpi$ yield a peak of around $16\, \mathrm{km\, s^{-1}}$, while the Bailer-Jones geometric distances $r_{\mathrm{geo}}$ yield around $12\, \mathrm{km\, s^{-1}}$. Minimizing the low-frequency power favors a solar radial motion of $U_\odot=10.8\, \mathrm{km\, s^{-1}}$ based on $d_\varpi$ and $U_\odot=10.4\, \mathrm{km\, s^{-1}}$ based on $r_{\mathrm{geo}}$. Collectively, the resulting spectrum establishes Gaia astrometry as a direct probe of disk-wide non-axisymmetric kinematics and provides quantitative targets for future dynamical modeling and interpretation.

title: Linear Stability, Inviscid Damping, and Scattering for Monotone Shear Flows in 2D Ideal MHD
abstract: We study the linearized 2D ideal incompressible magnetohydrodynamic equations around a monotone shear flow $(U(y),0)$ with a constant horizontal magnetic field $(β,0)$ on $\mathbb{T} \times \mathbb{R}$. For each fixed $β\neq 0$, we assume that the shear rate $U'$ is bounded above and below by positive constants and varies sufficiently slowly, although it need not be close to any constant. For every nontrivial perturbation with zero horizontal average, we establish sharp $L^2$ time rates in the corresponding paired norms: the horizontal velocity and magnetic components remain of order one, the vertical components decay at rate $\langle t \rangle^{-1}$, and the vorticity--current pair grows at rate $\langle t \rangle$. We prove strong $L^2$ scattering to two Alfvén profiles, identify the leading asymptotic behavior of the physical variables, and establish asymptotic completeness in the natural energy space.

title: On the Existence of Complete Coverings of Lee Spheres
abstract: Every perfect $r$-error-correcting Lee code in $\mathbb{Z}^n$ induces a finite configuration around each codeword: a family of pairwise disjoint radius-$r$ Lee spheres, all disjoint from the central sphere, that covers every lattice point at Lee distance $r+1$ from the codeword. We call such a configuration a complete covering. Under projection onto a suitable Cartesian product of cycles, a complete covering corresponds to an optimal local structure in the sense of Špacapan. The existence of a complete covering is necessary but, in general, not sufficient for the existence of a perfect Lee code, as our construction for $(n,r)=(3,2)$ shows. We prove that no complete covering exists whenever $n\ge 8$ and $r^2+\lfloor 25r/34\rfloor-3\ge 2n$. For the corresponding Cartesian products of cycles, this strengthens Špacapan's nonexistence theorem by replacing the linear radius condition $r\ge n$ with a threshold of order $\sqrt{2n}$. We also obtain an improved large-radius nonexistence bound for perfect Lee codes, strengthening the bound of Horak and Kim. Furthermore, we show that, for every $\varepsilon>0$, no complete covering exists when $n\ge 3$, $r$ is sufficiently large, and $r^2+(2/\mathrm{e}-\varepsilon)r\ge 2n$. On the positive side, we use near-optimal ternary constant-weight codes to construct almost complete coverings whose pairwise disjoint shadows cover a $1-o(1)$ proportion of the first outer Lee shell as the dimension tends to infinity, for every fixed radius.

title: Experimental Validation of Double-Blind Fourier Holography in an HWO-Like Segmented Aperture
abstract: Double-Blind Fourier Holography (DBFH) is a phase-retrieval method that has been shown numerically to address wavefront-sensing challenges for future segmented-aperture space telescopes, including the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO). DBFH uses a set of carefully selected pupil-plane amplitude masks and their corresponding focal-plane intensity measurements to construct an algebraically linear inverse problem, enabling computationally efficient and stable reconstruction of the complex pupil field. Here, we present the first experimental demonstration of DBFH using a spatial light modulator and an HWO EAC5-like segmented-aperture geometry. We reconstruct challenging pseudo-random wavefronts and compare DBFH with the established Focus-Diverse Phase Retrieval (FDPR) method. The two methods achieve comparable reconstruction precision, while exhibiting distinct strengths and limitations. We further demonstrate DBFH wavefront sensing in the presence of a binary source, a scenario that is not naturally accommodated by conventional FDPR. These results provide experimental proof of concept and establish technology readiness level 3 for DBFH as a wavefront-sensing method for space telescopes with segmented primary mirrors.

title: Attention under Bounded Key-Query Similarity: Space Complexity and Transformer Anisotropy
abstract: A growing body of work on KV-cache compression aims to reduce the memory requirements of autoregressive generation. These methods compress the stored context while approximately preserving attention computation, enabling generation with reduced memory consumption. Almost tight theoretical results on the worst case space complexity of attention have recently been obtained, but they are achieved by instances where queries can be perfectly aligned with keys. This directly contradicts the observed anisotropy of the key/query geometry in real transformers. In particular, it has been shown empirically that key/query cosine similarities are small even for most correlated pairs, i.e., near-perfect alignment of queries with keys does not happen in practice. In this paper, we study the space complexity of attention approximation under the assumption that key/query cosine similarities belong to a small interval around zero, i.e., a query cannot align too much with any key. We give a nearly space optimal algorithm and a corresponding space lower bound. Surprisingly, the distribution of key/query cosine similarities in our lower bound exhibits the anisotropy property empirically established and studied in the literature. Additionally, we show that the simple uniform sampling algorithm is nearly optimal for a typical range of parameters, supporting its surprising effectiveness on real datasets.

title: Revisiting supernova constraints on dark gauge bosons
abstract: We revisit the supernova constraints on three well-motivated light gauge bosons: the dark photon, the $U(1)_{B-L}$ gauge boson, and the $U(1)_{L_μ-L_τ}$ gauge boson. For the dark photon and the $U(1)_{B-L}$ gauge boson, we re-evaluate the nucleon bremsstrahlung process within the one-pion exchange approximation, retaining the full momentum and mass dependence. The geometrical dependence of the decay and absorption of these gauge bosons inside the supernova core is also taken into account. Updated bounds on these models are derived based on the cooling of SN1987A and energy deposition constraints from low-energy supernovae (LESNe). Taking the SFHo-18.8 $18.8\,M_\odot$ profile, the SN1987A cooling constraints reach masses of about $230$ MeV, $280$ MeV, and $300$ MeV for the dark photon, the $U(1)_{B-L}$ boson, and the $U(1)_{L_μ-L_τ}$ boson, while the corresponding LESN limits extend to about $450$ MeV, $440$ MeV, and $600$ MeV, respectively. The kinetic mixing parameter $ε$ for dark photon, the gauge coupling $g_{BL}$ in the $U(1)_{B-L}$ model, and the gauge coupling $g_{μτ}$ for the $U(1)_{L_μ-L_τ}$ model are constrained down to $5.8\times10^{-12}$, $2.9\times10^{-16}$, and $6.4\times10^{-12}$, respectively.

title: Convex orders in root systems and quantum tangent spaces
abstract: We classify the reduced decompositions of the longest element $w_0$ of the Weyl group of a semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ for which the corresponding Lusztig quantum root vectors span a quantum tangent space in $U_q(\mathfrak{g})$. We introduce a combinatorial condition on the convex order induced by a reduced decomposition, tangency, and prove that a reduced decomposition gives rise to a quantum tangent space if and only if it is tangent. The proof relies on a description of the coproduct of quantum root vectors in terms of the convex order, and on a projection in the right weak order attached to each positive root. Up to commutation, tangent reduced decompositions are obtained by concatenating the longest minimal coset representatives along a chain of cominuscule parabolic quotients; in particular there are none in types $E_8$, $F_4$ and $G_2$.

title: MoRE: Motion-Regularized Encoding for Articulated 3D Generation
abstract: Generating an articulated object from a single image requires recovering both its appearance and the mechanism governing its parts. A compact encoding of joint attributes does not by itself ensure that reconstruction preserves the resulting motion. We present MoRE, Motion-Regularized Encoding for articulated 3D generation. MoRE represents coordinate-aligned joint lines with axis classification and two axis-orthogonal Plücker moment coefficients, removing the arbitrary choice of an origin along the axis. During representation learning, decoded joint hypotheses are used to move corresponding three-dimensional anchors, and their motions are compared with those of annotated joints. A differentiable expectation over joint types and axis directions couples attribute reconstruction to the motion it induces. An image-conditioned flow learns the resulting functional latents, while a multi-state-adapted Gaussian model supplies appearance. At inference, recovered part assignments and joints articulate a single set of rest-pose Gaussians without regenerating the object for each state. Experiments on PartNet-Mobility and ACD show stronger part-box agreement, articulated-state geometry and visual similarity than the compared baselines, while joint prediction reduces axis, origin and range errors relative to ArtiLatent. Controlled ablations support the joint-line encoding and show that motion supervision reduces anchor-motion error. Code and pretrained checkpoints will be released in the future.

title: The Geometry of Agent Memory: Forecasting Retrieval-Bound Memory Failures, and Characterizing Its Limits
abstract: We study whether geometric relationships between conversation turns, memory texts, and queries can predict answer correctness before generation. We evaluate four memory implementations with dense or hybrid retrieval and one observation-summary comparator. We embed these texts in a shared space. A logistic classifier uses 25 features describing query proximity, memory-conversation correspondence, and conversation structure. On LongMemEval-small, pooled AUROC is 0.640 over 2,367 question-system pairs, below a question-difficulty baseline of 0.655. Performance varies by question type: geometry reaches 0.841 on single-session-assistant questions, but system identity alone reaches 0.826. After controlling for difficulty and identity, geometry adds no statistically established pooled improvement (delta = +0.002, 95% CI [-0.010, 0.014]). A fixed-store context-selection experiment finds higher accuracy with proximity-ranked memories than with random subsets, consistent with ordinary retrieval relevance. On LoCoMo, nearest-turn similarity has modest predictive value for single-hop questions and near-chance estimates for several other categories. Training uses correctness labels; prediction uses pre-answer features and no additional LLM generation call. The results characterize associations between memory representations and correctness, rather than establish a reliable deployment diagnostic. In particular, embedding proximity does not verify fact coverage or distinguish memory-construction, retrieval, and generation errors.

title: Biharmonic Conformal Immersions of Hypersurfaces: Dirac Rigidity and Mixed Clifford Geometry
abstract: A biharmonic conformal immersion asks whether a hypersurface can become a critical point of the bienergy after a conformal change of the domain metric. We study when this flexibility can produce compact nonconstant-mean-curvature geometry in space forms. For surfaces in three-dimensional space forms, with $U=λ^2H$, Ou's system is encoded exactly by a Laplace-type operator acting on a restricted ambient Killing spinor. We classify all monic scalar--chiral factorizations of this operator. In nonzero curvature such a factorization exists locally exactly when the principal curvatures are locally constant; the normalized Euclidean branch is equally rigid, and the remaining real spherical non-CMC branch is excluded by a finite-type Frobenius obstruction. For $m>2$, this scalar rigidity does not imply geometric nonexistence. The conformal tension has independent normal and tangential components. We prove that $\mathbb Rξ\oplus TM$ is the minimal natural $O(m)$-equivariant carrier, derive the corresponding strongly elliptic Jacobi block and its two-grade Clifford realization, and identify off-diagonal hybridization as the escape mechanism. Exact cohomogeneity-one reductions, combined with validated interval and Chebyshev/radii-polynomial arguments, yield embedded proper non-CMC, nowhere-umbilical examples in round spheres, including $$ S^1\times\mathbb S^n\times\mathbb S^n\hookrightarrow\mathbb S^{2n+2} \qquad(n\ge1). $$ Thus the scalar obstruction is sharp with respect to coefficient bundle: the smallest enlargement forced by conformal tension already supports compact non-CMC solutions.

title: WAVE: Wavelet-Controlled Coarse-to-Fine Guidance for Depth Super-Resolution
abstract: Guided depth super-resolution (GDSR) typically extracts RGB guidance features through convolutional hierarchies, inheriting their fine-to-coarse bias. Thus, low-level spatial cues surface in early layers, leaving the deeper layers to suppress those that do not correspond to true depth boundaries, which risks artifacts and blurred edges. The same fine-to-coarse bias persists in semantics-based methods that consume low-level tokens early and global tokens late. We present WAVE, which introduces a multi-level discrete wavelet transform (ML-DWT) as an explicit and interpretable feature-control mechanism, enabling a coarse-to-fine reconstruction by consuming sub-bands and semantic tokens in reverse of their generation order. WAVE further exploits these sub-bands to treat high- and low-frequency content separately, isolating the misleading RGB color and texture cues before any feature is learned so that their admission can be controlled explicitly, offering an intuitive alternative to the suppression learned implicitly by an opaque network. WAVE separates structure and detail reconstruction into dedicated modules that: i) model interactions within and across wavelet sub-bands, depth features, and semantic priors, ii) apply semantic gating to the high-frequency bands, and iii) fuse modalities through an invertible coupling mechanism that prevents collapse onto a single modality. Extensive experiments across multiple benchmarks demonstrate that WAVE matches or outperforms existing methods, with the largest gains at high upsampling factors, where low-resolution depth contains the least structure.

title: Decoherence of a quantum magneto-oscillator: Effect of field-bath interaction
abstract: We investigate the quantum dissipative dynamics of a charged magneto-oscillator(CMO) coupled to a heat bath of harmonic oscillators in the presence of an additional field-bath interaction. The problem is formulated within the framework of the generalized quantum Langevin equation, where the external confining potential modifies the random force correlations and the memory kernel of the environment, and the effective spring constant. Using the corresponding non-Markovian master equation, we examine the influence of the field-bath coupling on the temporal decay of the reduced density matrix of the system. We show that the additional interaction leads to an enhancement of the decoherence rate by altering the dissipative response of the bath. Thus our results shed light on the role of field-bath coupling in the quantum to classical transition of a CMO. The resulting fluctuation-dissipation relation is analyzed, and the position autocorrelation, position-velocity correlation and velocity autocorrelation are obtained explicitly. The dependence of these experimentally accessible quantities on the field-bath coupling parameter is discussed. We outline an experimental proposal for testing our theoretical predictions. The study sheds light on reservoir engineering which is central to quantum technologies.

title: Second order Recurrences, quadratic number fields and cyclic codes
abstract: Wall-Sun-Sun primes (shortly WSS primes) are defined as those primes $p$ such that the period of the Fibonacci recurrence is the same modulo $p$ and modulo $p^2.$ This concept has been generalized recently to certain second order recurrences whose characteristic polynomials admit as a zero the principal unit of $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{d}),$ for some integer $d>0.$ Primes of the latter type we call $WSS(d).$ They correspond to the case when $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{d})$ is not $p$-rational. For such a prime $p$ we study the weight distributions of the cyclic codes over $\mathbb{F}_p$ and $\mathbb{Z}_{p^2}$ whose check polynomial is the reciprocal of the said characteristic polynomial. Some of these codes are MDS (reducible case) or NMDS (irreducible case).

title: A generalization of pseudocomplementation in semilattices, lattices and posets with 0
abstract: Pseudocomplemented lattices satisfy a lot of nice properties and were studied by a number of algebraists. However, even when a poset P with 0 is not pseudocomplemented, we can assign to every element a of P the set $a^p$ of all maximal elements being orthogonal to a. This assignment $^p$ is a non-trivial operator provided P satisfies the so-called Ascending Chain Condition (ACC). In particular, we investigate this operator when the poset P in question is a semilattice or a lattice. We characterize this operator and describe its properties that turn out to be similar to the corresponding properties of pseudocomplementation. Moreover, we introduce an equivalence relation $Θ_p$ on P induced by $^p$ similarly as it was done by V. I. Glivenko for distributive pseudocomplemented lattices. Finally, we investigate for which lattices L with 0 satisfying the ACC this equivalence relation turns out to be a congruence and when the quotient lattice $L/Θ_p$ is complemented respectively modular.

title: Phonon number relaxation in a 3D superfluid with a concave acoustic branch
abstract: We consider the collisional evolution towards equilibrium of a spatially homogeneous and isotropic phonon gas of a three-dimensional superfluid with a concave acoustic excitation branch, at a non-zero but arbitrarily low temperature $T$. Three-phonon collisions $1φ\leftrightarrow 2φ$ are forbidden by conservation of energy-momentum. Four-phonon collisions $2φ\to 2φ$ of Landau and Khalatnikov lead, after a time $\propto T^{-7}$, only to a partial thermal equilibrium, a Bose law of non-zero chemical potential for the phonons, because they conserve the total number of phonons. Relaxation towards complete thermochemical equilibrium is therefore ensured by the much slower five-phonon collisions $2φ\leftrightarrow 3φ$ of Khalatnikov, in a time $\propto T^{-9}$. Using kinetic equations on the occupation numbers of the phonon modes and explicitly calculating the $2φ\to 3φ$ collisional amplitude with quantum hydrodynamics at low temperature, we determine the corresponding evolution of the fugacity $z_φ$ of the phonon gas from the non-degenerate regime $z_φ=0^+$ to complete equilibrium $z_φ=1^-$. Using the conservation of total energy, we find that the fugacity varies with a non-integer power law $\propto t^{4/5}$ at short times and an exponential law at long times; the speed of change of entropy, always positive, is asymptotically proportional to the square of the speed of change of fugacity, $(\mathrm{d}/\mathrm{d}t)S_φ\propto[(\mathrm{d}/\mathrm{d}t)z_φ]^2$, as Landau predicted for an arbitrarily slow adiabatic transformation. Our results bring to a close the study initiated by Khalatnikov in 1950 and could be experimentally verified in a gas of cold spin-1/2 fermionic atoms in the sector of the BEC-BCS crossover where the acoustic branch has a concave start, or in superfluid liquid helium-4 at sufficiently high pressure.

title: Quasinormal modes of thick branes in $f(R,T)$ gravity
abstract: We study tensor perturbations and quasinormal modes (QNMs) of thick branes in $f(R,T)=R+αT$ gravity. Starting from the background thick brane solutions, we derive the Schrödinger-like equation for gravitational perturbations and construct the corresponding effective potential. The effective potential exhibits a double-barrier structure whose properties depend on the model parameters. We analyze transmission spectra and find good agreement between resonance peaks and the real parts of the quasinormal frequencies. The parameters $b$ and $α$ mainly control the width and height of the potential barriers, respectively. QNMs are extracted using both time-domain evolution and direct integration methods, showing consistent results for low-lying modes. Higher overtones become increasingly difficult to extract due to stronger damping and numerical contamination. Our results indicate that $f(R,T)$ corrections significantly affect both the effective potential and the quasinormal spectrum, providing a possible imprint of modified gravity in braneworld perturbations.

title: Learning by Confusion Locates a Parametrization-Dependent Fisher Information Maximum
abstract: Learning by confusion (LBC) is a machine-learning method for locating phase transitions without assuming a known order parameter. Its characteristic accuracy curve contains a central maximum that is interpreted as the transition point, but what determines the location and finite-size scaling of this maximum has remained unclear. We derive an exact balance condition for the Bayes-optimal confusion peak and show that, for equilibrium systems with a single swept parameter, the peak closely follows the maximum of the corresponding Fisher information. This immediately gives its finite-size scaling and reveals an unexpected dependence on how the data are sampled: the same configurations arranged on grids uniform in $T$, $\ln T$, or $β=1/T$ can yield different finite-size pseudocritical trajectories. Tests on the Ising, Blume-Capel, Potts, and Baxter-Wu models confirm the prediction across continuous, tricritical, and first-order transitions. Our results identify the statistical quantity measured by LBC and show that finite-size machine-learning estimates can depend on the parametrization of the training data as well as on the underlying physics.

title: Faithful Localization of Vertex Algebra Modules
abstract: We establish a Faithfulness Theorem for vertex algebra modules, showing that two complementary geometric localizations can jointly detect global algebraic structure. We apply this principle to vertex algebras obtained by BRST reduction from classical invariant theory and identify them, under natural geometric hypotheses, with global sections of sheaves of chiral differential operators. As consequences, we prove vanishing of BRST cohomology in nonzero degrees and simplicity, and show that every finitely strongly generated module is a finite direct sum of copies of the vacuum module. In particular, the corresponding module category is equivalent to the category of finite-dimensional vector spaces. For families associated with classical groups, we identify the associated varieties with Hamiltonian reductions, proving quasi-lisse-ness and the predicted identification with Higgs branches of the corresponding supersymmetric gauge theories. This provides geometric realizations of a broad class of vertex algebras arising from three- and four-dimensional quantum field theories.

title: The maximum spectral radius of outerplanar and planar $k$-uniform hypergraphs
abstract: For $k\ge3$, a $k$-angulation is a simple $2$-connected outerplane graph whose interior faces are bounded by $k$-cycles, and a closed $k$-angulation is a simple $2$-connected plane graph all of whose faces are bounded by $k$-cycles. Their face hypergraphs have the same vertices as the graphs; the hyperedges are the vertex sets of the interior faces, respectively all faces. For $k=3$, the extremal problems over these hypergraphs agree with those for the outerplanar and planar $3$-uniform hypergraphs of Ellingham, Lu and Wang, who determined the outerplanar maximizer for large $n$ and conjectured the planar one. In this paper, for each fixed $k$, we determine the hypergraphs of maximum spectral radius in both classes for all sufficiently large $n$ satisfying the corresponding face-count divisibility condition. In the outerplanar case, the unique extremal hypergraph is the face hypergraph of the fan, in which one vertex lies on every interior face. In the planar case with $k=3$, it is the face hypergraph of $K_2+P_{n-2}$, which confirms the conjecture of Ellingham, Lu and Wang. For $k\ge4$, the extremal hypergraphs are the face hypergraphs of balanced theta graphs, in which two vertices lie on every face. For $k=4$, the result holds for every $n\ge5$, with extremal hypergraph ${\mathcal H}(K_{2,n-2})$. For $k\ge6$ and an even number of faces, there are exactly $\lfloor(k-2)/2\rfloor$ extremal hypergraphs up to isomorphism.

title: Revisiting the Schwarz Lemma for the Pentablock: Counterexamples and Sharp Interpolation Criteria
abstract: Alshehri and Lykova (\emph{J. Geom. Anal.} \textbf{33} (2023)) formulated a Schwarz lemma for the pentablock $P$, giving a criterion for the existence of an analytic map from the unit disc $\mathbb D$ into the closed pentablock $\overline P$ that sends the origin to the origin and a prescribed point $λ_0\in\mathbb D$ to a given point $x_0\in\overline P$. We show that the sufficiency direction of their criterion is false. We identify the underlying error as the extension to the open unit disc of a Fejér--Riesz identity that is valid only on the unit circle. We establish a corrected necessary and sufficient interpolation criterion when the last two components are prescribed by a fixed rational $Γ$-inner function and resolve the special case $s_0=0$. Using the Poisson integral representation of the associated outer spectral factor, we obtain a sharp comparison between the corrected bound and the bound proposed by Alshehri and Lykova, with a precise characterization of equality. We further express the logarithmic difference between these bounds as a nonnegative Green potential, thereby quantifying the discrepancy in terms of the derivative of the first coordinate of the prescribed $Γ$-inner function. Finally, we formulate a variational problem over rational $Γ$-inner interpolants satisfying the prescribed two-point conditions. We show that the supremum of the associated outer-factor quantities determines the maximal admissible modulus of the first coordinate among pentablock-valued interpolants whose last two components belong to this class. Equivalently, this extremal problem reduces to minimizing the corresponding Green potential. We conclude by discussing the remaining problem of characterizing unrestricted Schwarz interpolation for the pentablock and its connection with the Lempert function.

title: Effects of Pulse Duration on Kerr Self-Focusing and Weld Formation in Ultrafast Laser Welding of Fused Silica
abstract: Kerr self-focusing can shift the laser interaction region away from the geometrical focus, making energy deposition near the joining interface difficult to control. Here, the effect of pulse duration on nonlinear focusing and weld formation is investigated from 262 fs to 10 ps. ICCD imaging shows clear changes in the axial position and shape of the plasma emission. Different pulse durations already produce distinct axial positions during the initial 2000 pulses, and these positions continue to evolve with pulse accumulation. The final weld morphology, weld position, and shear strength show corresponding changes. A ray-optics model including the Kerr effect is used to calculate the focal shift. The simulated trend agrees with the experiment and supports the role of Kerr self-focusing in the observed focal position change. These results clarify the relationship between pulse duration, nonlinear focusing, interaction position, and weld formation.

title: An asymptotically conical regular black hole in four-dimensional nonpolynomial quasitopological gravity
abstract: In this work, we construct an asymptotically conical regular black hole in four-dimensional nonpolynomial quasitopological gravity. Starting from a linear choice of the reduced function, which yields an asymptotically conical Schwarzschild-like solution, we introduce a nonlinear deformation that preserves the leading asymptotic cone while producing an exact black hole solution with a de Sitter core and finite curvature invariants. We further establish the corresponding black hole thermodynamics for both solutions within the Hamiltonian and Wald frameworks. The entropy contains rational and logarithmic terms in the regular model, and both solutions satisfy the first law of black hole thermodynamics.

title: PPT-assisted capacities of bosonic Gaussian channels
abstract: We determine the exact quantum communication and entanglement-distribution capacities of three fundamental bosonic channels, namely thermal loss, thermal amplification and additive Gaussian noise, assisted by operations that completely preserve positive partial transpose (PPT). These operations are more powerful than local operations and classical communication (LOCC), but cannot generate distillable entanglement on their own. For thermal loss, the unconstrained capacity coincides with the Pirandola-Laurenza-Ottaviani-Banchi (PLOB) bound throughout the non-entanglement-breaking regime. The corresponding upper bounds are also attained for thermal amplification and additive noise. We extend these results to energy-constrained communication, establishing exact capacities for all three channels at every prescribed mean input energy. Our results solve a class of bosonic capacity problems under PPT assistance and establish exact benchmarks for determining whether the same communication rates can be achieved via LOCC alone.

title: Infinite-Particle Determinantal Dynamics from Brownian Motion on $\mathrm{GL}_N(\mathbb{C})$
abstract: We study the edge scaling limit of the logarithms of the squared singular values of multiplicative Brownian motion on the general linear group $\mathrm{GL}_N(\mathbb{C})$ with general initial conditions. Building on earlier work [arXiv:2605.06429], we prove that, for every initial condition in the enhanced state space, the limiting dynamics are determinantal and derive an explicit double-contour formula for their extended multitime correlation kernel. The dependence on the initial state, including information not determined by the particle coordinates, is encoded by the associated Laguerre--Pólya entire function. We further extend the construction of solutions to the corresponding infinite-dimensional system of singular stochastic differential equations to arbitrary initial configurations, including those with coinciding coordinates.

title: BFLA: Block-Filtered Long-Context Attention Mechanism
abstract: We propose Block-Filtered Long-Context Attention (BFLA), a training-free sparse prefill method that combines deterministic Lightning-style block indexing, query-tile sharing, and length-adaptive Ratio-$K$ selection with block-sparse execution. BFLA evaluates attention using the original Q/K/V, requires no retraining or per-model parameter retuning, and integrates with vLLM while preserving native decoding. For fixed Q/K/V, we bound local attention-output error in terms of the omitted attention mass, indexer-score distortion, retention budget, and query-tile sharing. Evaluations on Gemma4-E4B-IT, Qwen3.6-27B, Qwen3.8-27B, and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next across LongBench-v2, RULER, InfiniteBench, and Terminal Bench 2.1 show BFLA matches or even outperforms dense baselines. BFLA shows up to approximately $4\times$ time-to-first-token and $3.72\times$ end-to-end request speedups over the corresponding dense-prefill baselines. Comparisons with state-of-the-art FlashPrefill V2 and Qwen Sparse Attention also demonstrate that BFLA has better performance and efficiency trade-offs. These findings highlight the value of BFLA for the acceleration of long-context serving. Project website: https://github.com/Alicewithrabbit/BFLA.

title: Theory and Cosmology of Biverse Volume-Normalized Gravity
abstract: This dissertation expounds the biverse volume-normalized gravity, a novel theoretical framework of classical and quantum gravity that provides an unusual solution to the cosmological constant problem, the 60-degree-of-magnitude discrepancy between the value of the vacuum energy density in our universe predicted by particle physics and that implied by cosmological data. In the literature, there exist two interesting ideas: 1) to use the "volume-normalized" action functional, the usual action of the particle Standard Model and general relativity but divided by the spacetime volume, first proposed by Tseytlin; 2) to generate the vacuum energy density dynamically by assigning a ghost-free massive potential to the graviton. However, each has a problem: Tseytlin's attempt suffers from diverging quantum loops and the massive gravity theory has a second metric tensor with questionable origin and the quantum strong coupling problem. Inspired by these two ideas, as well as the AdS/CFT correspondence in string theory, the biverse volume-normalized gravity extends Tseytlin's idea by placing our (3+1)-dimensional universe on the boundary of a (4+1)-dimensional bulk space. This new adaptation controls the large quantum gravity loops in the limit of vanishing ratio of the spacetime volume of our universe to that of the other universe. The ghost-free massive gravity can then be seamlessly incorporated, not only that its otherwise nebulous second metric tensor appears naturally as the pullback of the bulk metric on the boundary, but its strong coupling problem also solved. The biverse volume-normalized gravity is also consistent with all tested models of particle cosmology and the evolution of the universe, and nontrivially predicts that the tensor-to-scalar ratio of our universe is exactly zero.

title: Unique direct-sum decompositions of infinite-dimensional unitary representations of the infinite dihedral group via real CMV matrices
abstract: Unitary representations of the infinite dihedral group arise naturally and play an important role in a wide range of areas including mathematics, physics, and engineering. CMV matrices, introduced by Cantero, Moral, and Velázquez, are five-diagonal unitary matrices that are standard tools in the theory of orthogonal polynomials on the unit circle. It is known that every unitary representation of the infinite dihedral group on a separable Hilbert space admits a discrete direct-sum decomposition into representations arising from the natural factorizations of real CMV matrices and copies of two exceptional one-dimensional irreducible representations. We prove that such a decomposition is unique up to unitary equivalence when the summands arising from real CMV matrices are grouped according to their multiplicities and the spectral measures of the corresponding matrices are mutually singular across distinct multiplicities. Furthermore, we show that the representation associated with each such real CMV matrix $C$ admits a direct integral decomposition into irreducible unitary representations with respect to the push-forward of the restriction of the spectral measure of $C$ to the closed upper half circle. These results make it possible to study the structure of unitary representations of the infinite dihedral group using CMV matrices and the theory of orthogonal polynomials on the unit circle.

title: The Integrable Snake Model
abstract: A pure snake configuration is a bijection $σ:\mathbb{Z}^2 \to \mathbb{Z}^2$ containing no two-cycles and such that for each $x \in \mathbb{Z}^2$ we have $σ(x) \in \{ x , x+ \mathbf{e}^1, x+\mathbf{e}^2 , x- \mathbf{e}^2 \}.$ The non-trivial cycles of a pure snake configuration may be regarded as a collection of non-intersecting paths in $\mathbb{Z}^2$ that may travel right, up, or down (but not left) from a given vertex. Pure snake configurations are a generalisation of lozenge tilings, which are in natural correspondence with paths that only travel right or up. We introduce a partition function on a finite version of this model and study the probabilistic properties of random pure snake configurations chosen according to their contribution to this partition function. Under a suitable weighting, the model is integrable in the sense that we have access to explicit formulas for its partition function and correlation function. We utilise the integrable structure of this model in several applications through its various scaling limits, such as to prove a traffic representation of ASEP on the ring, generalising the analogous result for TASEP by the first author.

title: Low Genus Curves on Compact Shimura Surfaces
abstract: We investigate and compare the behaviors of complex curves on two major types of compact Shimura surfaces: compact variants of Picard and Hilbert modular surfaces. They are quotients of complex hyperbolic balls corresponding to moduli problems for abelian varieties with certain endomorphism types. We prove that if we fix a genus bound, then when the defining discriminant is large enough, low genus curves on the compact variant of Picard modular surfaces do not exist, while low genus curves may persist on the compact variant of Hilbert modular surfaces only if they are special curves, which parametrize those with extra endomorphisms. These results are special cases of a complex function field analogue of uniform boundedness on endomorphism types of abelian varieties. The proof requires understanding the repulsion of special subvarieties and relies on volume estimates in hyperbolic geometry.

title: Trivial topology-entailed states at interfaces between identical topological phases
abstract: Topological edge states arise at boundaries between bulk phases with distinct topological invariants and are characterized by robust, often chiral transport. When two domains sharing identical bulk topology are brought into contact, their counterpropagating edge modes are generally expected to hybridize and cancel each other out in the process. Here, we show that this cancellation can be lifted by trivial parameter variations at the interface, giving rise to a distinct class of gap-localized inter-face modes, which we term trivial topology-entailed (TTE) states. Using anomalous Floquet photonic lattices as a concrete platform, we experimentally observe the formation of bidirectional TTE states between topologically equivalent domains. In particular, we demonstrate their spectral confinement within bulk gaps, their coherent coupling to conventional chiral edge channels, and their ability to mediate interface-guided transport across composite lattices. Our results establish TTE states as a general interface phenomenon in composite topological systems and provide a unified framework for understanding hybridized boundary modes beyond conventional bulk-boundary correspondence.

title: A discrete series gauge field at the late-time boundary of $dS_4$
abstract: We study the free Maxwell field on the planar patch of four-dimensional de Sitter spacetime ($dS_4$). We review its bulk canonical quantization in the Bunch-Davies vacuum, and we give a representation-theoretic viewpoint by studying the transformation properties of single-particle states under infinitesimal dS transformations. By taking the late-time limit, we identify two late-time operators with scaling dimensions $Δ=1$ (leading) and $Δ=2$ (subleading). We introduce CFT-inspired inner products invariant under the dS group ($SO(4,1)$) for states created by late-time operators acting on the Bunch-Davies vacuum. We explain how the unitary discrete series representations of $SO(4,1)$ associated with the photon are furnished by both operators, in contrast with the Maxwell field on $AdS$ where the $Δ=1$ operator corresponds to a non-normalizable mode. We also explain how the corresponding discrete series representations of $SO(4,1)$ split into a direct sum of representations corresponding to two helicities $+1$ and $-1$.
